Shasta County CA Tax Sale – Make Your Money Work for You

Thinking about buying property in Northern California without spending a fortune? Shasta County’s tax-defaulted property auctions might be a great opportunity for you. These sales let investors buy real estate at low prices while helping the county recover unpaid property taxes.

Here’s everything you need to know in one place.

Shasta County Tax Sale – Key Information

How the Tax Auction Works

First, you’ll need to register on the Bid4Assets website. During registration, you must submit a refundable $5,000 deposit and pay a $35 fee. After that, you’ll be allowed to participate in the auction.

Each property starts with a minimum bid. These bids cover unpaid taxes, penalties, and auction fees. Once you place a bid, you can continue bidding during the auction window until it closes.

If you win, you must pay the full amount within three business days. The county accepts only wire transfers or certified checks. No personal checks or credit cards are allowed.

After full payment is received, the Tax Deed to Purchaser is recorded within ten business days. The deed is held for 30 days and then mailed to the new owner.

Important Things to Know Before You Bid

These properties are sold as-is. That means no inspections, no guarantees, and no warranties from the county. Some properties might have other legal issues, code violations, or existing liens.

Also, property owners have the right to pay off their back taxes and remove the property from the auction. This can happen up until 5 PM the business day before the auction starts.

It’s also possible for auctions to be postponed or cancelled. So keep checking for updates before you bid.

Why Shasta County is a Smart Place to Invest

Affordable Housing

Home prices in Shasta County are much more affordable than other parts of California. While California’s average home price is over $700,000, you can still find homes in Redding and nearby areas for around $350,000 to $400,000.

Rental Demand is Steady

Shasta County’s population is growing, but new housing hasn’t kept up. This means demand for rentals is strong—especially in cities like Anderson and Redding. Investors looking for long-term rentals should take notice.

Location and Outdoor Appeal

Shasta County is filled with natural beauty. It’s home to places like Lassen Volcanic National Park, Shasta Lake, and Whiskeytown Lake. People love the area for outdoor fun like hiking, fishing, and camping.

This natural setting also makes the county a good option for vacation rentals or Airbnb properties.

Fire Risk and Local Changes

Northern California has seen more wildfires in recent years, and Shasta County is no exception. As a result, there have been changes to local zoning rules and insurance requirements. If you’re planning to buy property in a high-risk area, check with the county for any updates before bidding.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

Do I have to live in California to bid?
No. Anyone can bid, including people from out of state or outside the U.S.

Are these properties guaranteed to be free of liens or problems?
No. The county does not offer any guarantees. You should research each property before bidding to check for liens, zoning issues, or code violations.

Can I see the property before I buy?
Usually no. Many of these properties are still occupied or fenced. You can view them from public streets but cannot go onto the property.

What if the owner pays their taxes right before the auction?
If that happens, the property is removed from the sale list and will not be auctioned.

What happens if I win the auction but don’t pay on time?
You lose the property and your $5,000 deposit.

Pro Tips for New Investors

  • Research the property using county GIS maps and tax records.
  • Always double-check zoning laws if you have plans to build or rent.
  • Look for properties near high-demand areas like Redding or near lakes and parks.
  • Read the Bid4Assets terms before registering.
